subject: Privatenet readiness: hosting choice, PrivateLink vs peering, and allowlist action
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@opticlient.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Network Team <network@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Privatenet readiness: hosting choice, PrivateLink vs peering, and allowlist action

Thanks again for your time today, Alex — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move the deployment decision (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) to a firm recommendation for the SOW.

Call recap (high level)
- OptiClient confirmed the priority is data isolation + predictable latency for inference workloads.
- You indicated a preference leaning toward a Private VPC deployment (either PrivateLink or VPC peering) instead of Hosted API.
- Procurement asked for clear networking asks and a short timeline for on-boarding once we finalize approach.

Open decisions we need to resolve
1) PrivateLink vs VPC peering — tradeoffs (connectivity model, egress ownership, on-prem NAT concerns). Owner: Redwood (Mina) to propose default. Due: 2026-09-04 EOD.
2) Egress IP model — will OptiClient provide a fixed NAT IP block for our outbound calls (if peering) or will PrivateLink be required to avoid egress? Owner: OptiClient NetOps to confirm. Due: 2026-09-06.
3) Allowlist items — exact CIDR/IPs + FQDNs + ports. Owner: Ben (Redwood) to send a first-pass checklist. Due: 2026-09-04.
4) Timeline for SOW signature and onboarding windows (preferred go-live target). Owner: OptiClient procurement + Redwood sales. Proposed: sign by 2026-09-24 to start provisioning.

Attachments attached to this thread: redwood_privatelink_vs_peering.pdf (short decision matrix), sow_draft_opticlient.pdf (initial SOW draft).

Immediate asks for OptiClient NetOps
- Please share a technical contact + preferred calendar slots for a 45m NetOps deep-dive next week.
- Confirm whether you can provide a static egress IP block (or an explanation of your NAT topology) if we choose peering.

Next steps (my proposal)
- Ben will push a concise network checklist (CIDRs, ports, FQDNs) by EOD 2026-09-04.
- I will send the PrivateLink vs Peering decision matrix and schedule a NetOps call for the week of 9/7.
- Procurement: please review the SOW draft and flag any high-level legal/commerce items; we'll convert to DocuSign once network approach is agreed.

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_privatelink_vs_peering.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB), sow_draft_opticlient.pdf (DOCX, 28 KB)

From: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@opticlient.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: NetOps <netops@opticlient.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privatenet readiness: hosting choice, PrivateLink vs peering, and allowlist action

Thanks Mina — great summary. Confirming a few points from our side: we are leaning to a Private VPC deployment and prefer PrivateLink if it avoids additional NAT/egress configuration on our side. Main constraints to flag:

- We currently have strict outbound NAT rules; handing over a static egress block for peering would require an internal change request and may take multiple weeks.
- Our preferred NetOps contact is Priya Nair (priya.nair@opticlient.com). She is cc'd on this note.
- We can provide a list of existing firewall egress rules but not a static NAT range immediately.

Action items from OptiClient
- Priya will coordinate availability for a 45m NetOps session next week (aiming for 9/8–9/10).
- We'll review the SOW draft and respond with procurement timing by 9/10.

See my inline note quoting your recap below.

Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privatenet readiness: hosting choice, PrivateLink vs peering, and allowlist action

Alex — perfect, thanks for the quick confirmation and for looping Priya in. Priya, welcome — we'll keep this short and technical on the NetOps call.

Ben and I discussed and attached a short matrix (redwood_privatelink_vs_peering.pdf) that outlines:
- When we recommend PrivateLink vs Peering (customer NAT complexity, egress ownership, monitoring/traceability)
- Differences in rollout steps and typical provisioning lead times

Immediate asks from OptiClient NetOps (what we'd like before the deep-dive)
- Any internal change request or RFC numbers that would impact the ability to allocate static egress IPs. If that is going to be >2 weeks, call out early (will push us to PrivateLink).
- A sample firewall rule set (outbound) or a short list of existing egress restrictions so we can see if additional ports need to be opened.

Proposed NetOps deep-dive agenda (45m)
- 10m: topology review (OptiClient on-prem / VPC setup)
- 20m: PrivateLink vs peering technical walk-through + implications for routing/egress
- 10m: allowlist items and change-window constraints
- 5m: next steps and owners

I'll send a calendar invite once Priya suggests availability. If you want Ben or Laura to prepare anything specific on the deep-dive, flag it here.

Thanks, Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_privatelink_vs_peering.pdf (decision matrix)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@opticlient.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privatenet readiness: hosting choice, PrivateLink vs peering, and allowlist action

Alex / Priya — looping in a concise network checklist we use for Private VPC onboarding. I've filled in the items we can provide now; please confirm the OptiClient values in-line where noted.

Redwood private VPC onboarding checklist (first pass)
- Deployment model: PrivateLink preferred (if OptiClient cannot commit to static egress CIDR within 2 weeks).
- Required outbound ports: 443 (HTTPS) to our control plane and model endpoints; 853/53 (DNS) if internal name resolution to privatelink hostnames is needed; 123 (NTP) optional for long-running hosts.
- Hostnames/FQDNs to allow: privatelink.us.redwood-inference.com, control.redwood-inference.com.
- Egress IPs/CIDRs (Redwood-managed): 34.210.128.0/26 (sample; final to be confirmed after we choose region).
- Customer-provided egress (if peering): [OPTICLIENT_TO_FILL] — need static NAT block or clear RFC.
- Ports inbound from Redwood (if peering): none expected — traffic is initiated from your side toward our endpoints.
- TLS & certs: Redwood provides service certs for the privatelink endpoints; mutual TLS optional for private peering.
- Monitoring/tracing: We will enable request-level trace IDs and can send logs to a covered S3 bucket or via syslog integration (agreement required).

Action items
- Priya: please confirm whether OptiClient can provide a static egress block (add to thread) or mark as "will not be available".
- Priya / Alex: share 2–3 time slots for the NetOps deep-dive (9/8–9/10 preferred).
- Mina / Ben: we'll prepare a trimmed SOW and push to DocuSign pending decision on PrivateLink vs peering.

DocuSign SOW link (draft): https://docusign.com/embedded/abcdef123456
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345
